newsitem.title: UK: SAC 1997 sugar production seen highest for decade.
newsitem.headline: SAC 1997 sugar production seen highest for decade.

text.p: Sugar output in Caribbean sugar economies should rise by 47,000 tonnes to 874,000 tonnes in 1997, the highest in the last decade, the Sugar Association of the Caribbean (SAC) said on Monday.
"The continuing upswing in production confirms the optimistic outlook for the future," a SAC statement said.
The SAC expected to meet all of the Caricom region's demand for sugar in the near futures as well as continuing to meet export quotas, it added.
The SAC is a grouping within the Africa, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) sugar growers' body.
Sugar Protocol and Special Preferential Sugar (SPS) quotas allocated to the SAC would amount to 530,000 tonnes in 1996/97 and were expercted to remain the same in the 1997/98 delivery period.
The SAC said it had been allocated 101,500 tonnes out of the total 2.1 million tonnes of sugar allocated by the U.S. for the 1996/97 marketing year under its new administrative imports programme.
This was higher than the 85,146 tonnes initially allocated, while further allocations were expected before the end of the quota year, it said.
In 1996, the SAC received a U.S. quota allocation of 110,977 tonnes, compared with 72,651 tonnes in 1995.

Sugar exports to the European Union totalled 558,914 tonnes in 1996 compared with 422,328 tonnes in 1995, providing the region with some $404 million in foreign exchange earnings in 1996 after $300 million in 1995.
The directors of the SAC held their 120th meeting in Barbados on May 8 and 9, the statement said.
